# v0.25.1 — recall: natural-language queries with embeddings off (#864, #870, #873, #874)

Patch release on top of `v0.25.0` (`67de214f`), cut from the `release/v0.25.x` branch. It carries one fix,
the `lcm_recall` full-text change merged to `main` as #870 and #874, byte-identical to `main` in every file it
touches, plus the version identity and this file. Nothing else from `main` is included.

Why a patch: `lcm_recall` documents "ask in natural language", and embeddings are off by default. With
embeddings off, `v0.25.0` turned a natural-language question into an implicit AND of every word, sorted newest
first, so a typical question matched only large tool outputs that happen to contain every word, or nothing.
Policy H normally keeps a non-respin defect for the next minor; this patch is a recorded exception because it
restores a documented contract, touches only the recall full-text arm, and `v0.26.0` has no date yet.

- No tool name or count changed (15 tools); `LCM plugin loaded` and every `lcm_*` name are unchanged.
- **Store:** no schema version change (schema 5), no new table and no new column; `db_bootstrap.py` and
  `store.py` are unchanged since `v0.25.0`. A rollback to `v0.25.0` is plugin-only.
- No new environment key. No change below deletes or rewrites a stored row; recall is read-only.
- This release never moves a deployed pin by itself. A deployment moves only when its operator re-pins it.

## Changes since v0.25.0

- **Fix (#864, #870):** the full-text arm of `lcm_recall` now sends the question's content words to SQLite FTS5
  as one OR expression and ranks the hits by relevance (BM25) instead of recency.
  - Stop words and the tokenizer's contraction tails are dropped; each remaining word is split on the boundary the
    full-text index uses, so the arm searches tokens the index actually holds.
  - A question that contains emoji keeps the earlier LIKE route, now ranked by relevance.
  - `lcm_grep`, explicit full-text queries and the embedding arms are unchanged. The OR form is reachable only from
    `lcm_recall`; `lcm_grep` drops the internal flag before it dispatches.
- **Fix (#873, #874):** follow-ups from review of #870.
  - A phrase the question quotes stays one quoted phrase, stop words included.
  - An exact `NOT` or `NEAR` is quoted, so it is searched as a word, never parsed as an operator.
  - Case duplicates fold to the first spelling.
  - The answer-ready window centres on a phrase matched across punctuation and line breaks, the way FTS5 matches it.
- **Ranking change, stated plainly:** with embeddings off, recall results move from newest-first to most-relevant
  first. With embeddings on, the full-text arm now contributes relevance-ranked candidates to the fused ranking.

## Qualification

- **Same code as reviewed `main`:** both fixes were reviewed at their exact heads on `main` (#870, #874; cross-model
  review and a bot round on each), and the five files they touch are byte-identical to `main` at `c75313dc`.
- **Release delta review:** a cross-model review (Codex gpt-6.1-sol, high effort) checked the version identity,
  the documentation and these notes against the measurement evidence. Its first round found four text errors (a
  mixed denominator, a data-handling sentence, a release-versus-`main` identity sentence and an unqualified #387
  sentence); all are corrected, and the second round passed.
- **Tests:** full suite on this branch, the CI way: 5,671 passed, 92 skipped, 16 xfailed, 0 failed; ruff clean.
- **CI:** `ci.yml` passed on this release's commit (dispatched on `release/v0.25.x`).
- **Recall measurements on a copy of an internal reference agent's store** (about 500,000 messages; only aggregate
  counts and timings are published; with embeddings on, the questions were embedded through the store's configured
  cloud embedding provider, as recall itself does). Receipt:
  [`V0251-GATES-RECEIPT.md`](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/releases/download/v0.25.1/V0251-GATES-RECEIPT.md).
  - Synthetic natural-language questions, embeddings off: `v0.25.0` returned hits for 17 of 20 questions, mostly
    large tool outputs (25 of 112 hits were user or assistant messages), and nothing for 3; this release returned
    hits for 20 of 20, 103 of 160 from user or assistant messages. A known-item probe found its source message in
    0 of 30 cases on `v0.25.0` and 6 of 30 on this release.
  - The agent's own recall questions, replayed with embeddings off (37 distinct calls): `v0.25.0` found nothing
    for 16 of them, and 11 of its 56 hits were user or assistant messages; this release found hits for all 37, 123
    of 277 from user or assistant messages.
  - The same 37 calls with embeddings on (full-text and summary vectors fused, on a copy whose vectors were
    re-keyed to the current privacy revision): questions with no hit went from 2 to 0, the user and assistant
    share from 90 of 278 hits to 114 of 296, and messages the agent later opened appeared in the top eight for 3 of
    4 instead of 2 of 4. The 20 synthetic questions returned the same top eight on both versions with embeddings on.
  - Full-text arm time on real questions: median about 0.5 s, up from a few milliseconds, because an OR query
    matches far more rows; the slowest, a 24-word question, took 2.2 s. With embeddings off the arm has the whole
    8 s recall deadline. With embeddings on its share is about 2 s, and that question came within 0.1 s of it; a
    capped arm is reported in coverage and the vector arms still answer (#881).
- **Not run:** the release gauntlet, because no compaction, store, schema or ingest code changed. An internal
  reference agent runs this release with a short watch and a live `lcm_recall` turn before the managed-profile pin
  moves; that watch is shorter than the 24 h soak a minor gets.

## Known follow-ups

- #881: bound the OR query's cost for long questions (fewer, rarer terms), so the full-text arm keeps headroom
  with embeddings on.
- #387 (unchanged by this release): with embeddings on and a cloud embedding provider, a store whose registered
  embedding profile carries an older privacy revision (registered before `v0.23.2`) makes `lcm_recall` fail with an
  embedding-privacy error, and the call returns no hits. `/lcm embed warmup` registers the current revision, after
  which recall answers from full text; `/lcm embed backfill --apply` then rebuilds the summary vectors (a summary the
  privacy check refuses currently fails its whole batch, #759). Local embedding providers skip this check, and
  embeddings are off by default.
- #875: recall centring and emoji follow-ups from the #874 review (four items; none returns wrong rows).
- #876: whether a NumPy runtime dependency should be declared (the outside float32 loader in #834).
- `v0.26.0` (on `main`, not in this patch): host message identity in shadow mode, the #821 re-land with its fixes
  (#877, #879), and the follow-ups #878 and #880.
- Known follow-ups listed for `v0.25.0` still apply: #626, #824, #823, #800, #727, #725, #775, #7, #827.

## Benchmark boundary

- The recall measurements above are a release smoke on one store, not a retrieval or QA benchmark claim. The recall
  re-baseline on the shipped default configuration runs on its own track (#812).

## Upgrade

- Plugin only: verify the exact commit, install this tag at it and restart the gateway. The store needs no
  migration. A rollback to `v0.25.0` is plugin-only.
- No setting changes. Agents keep asking `lcm_recall` in natural language; short keyword queries also work.
- If an operator watches recall latency: the full-text arm still runs on its own read-only connection under the
  recall deadline. An arm that runs past it is interrupted and reported in the result's coverage, without blocking
  the turn.
